Behaviour audit · 27 October 2026 · full report, revision 2

Close the daily workflow gaps before another chrome pass

Islam's “2026 editor with 2001 functionality” verdict identifies a real product problem: many ordinary actions between capable systems are incomplete. The remedy is to finish daily workflows and shared interaction contracts, then prove them through the native event paths.

Scope: editor, ara-editor-gpu, native UI, Hub, installation/update, project/export layout and Mac game UI input. Comparison: Unity 6000.3 LTS through 6000.7 beta, and UE 5.7. No Cargo commands, application launches or new native windows were used. Only this report was changed in the repository.

Read-only baseline: 81c0b8e95baf0323cd5f9e0772918f167d003ddc. The requested D:/Coding/projects/desktop/snengine and this worktree matched that clean commit when inspection began. Findings do not assert that the in-progress Lead A/B branches still contain these gaps. Early top-20 handoff was published as version 1 at this same URL.

VerdictEvidenceViewportHierarchyInspectorAssetsPlayConsolePrefabsLook developmentGeneralHubUpdatesDisk/exportMac inputShared UI fixesSprint + journeysAra’s edgeSources

1. Ten-line verdict

  1. Mac game UI is a reported blocker; the input path strongly suggests Retina coordinates are not converted to the UI space.
  2. Installed export can dead-end on missing player resources; the supplied runs prove both successful shipping and a repeatable packaging failure state.
  3. Assets cannot be safely reorganized through the editor: general rename, move, duplicate and delete remain unavailable.
  4. Scene assembly lacks orthographic editing, surface/vertex snap, marquee and duplicate-drag; even camera-speed controls do not affect fly movement.
  5. Drag/drop is a collection of narrow handlers: selected sets, entity-reference fields, folder moves and reliable reorder targets are incomplete.
  6. Detach-anything excludes Scene, and multiplayer Play shows one selected client rather than the simultaneous viewports required by D19.
  7. Live patch and Keep Changes exist below the UI; runtime inspection, simulate and possess/eject do not form a finished human workflow.
  8. Inspector collections stop at 32 items; nested prefab application, variants and atomic prefab undo need complete authoring journeys.
  9. Shared UI contracts are inconsistent: oversized overlays, ad hoc choice rows, unused modal support and different native-input paths recur across products.
  10. Preserve the working foundations—typed ops, schema tools, graphs, profiler, C# reload and MCP—and spend the next sprint closing complete daily tasks.

Evidence and confidence

Source means the implementation path was inspected. Capture proves visible state. Journey means a supplied run reported its assertions; it is not an independent rerun. Candidate marks a static explanation awaiting runtime confirmation. Absence claims are limited to the inspected editor/Hub registry and dispatch paths; lower-level engine support is called out separately.

No crash was reproduced, no installed app version was exercised, and no new performance measurement was taken. In particular, the Mac coordinate mismatch is a strong diagnosis candidate for Islam's reported failure; spontaneous Hub application remains unconfirmed in this source. Product-wide reliability and accessibility compliance cannot be inferred from captures.

Locked decisions: decisions D19–D28:27 and milestones:89. D19 requires both same-process and per-player-process Play, per-client views and conditions. D20 technical non-disruption still applies; D24 removes approval/idle queues and claims. D28 replaces D23 native-caption/nine-menu requirements but keeps floating windows and the shared command registry. D25 keeps one Hub/global MCP and side-by-side pins.

The Unity reference clone was present at bf6028387a4fc2ea6d41aa7d8998e774655aedf6. SceneViewMotion, TreeViewController, ProjectBrowser and PrefabOverridesWindow were studied for navigation, selection and source/instance patterns. No Unity/Flax/Unreal code was transcribed. No UE clone was present in the inspected .refs directory; comparisons use version-pinned Epic documentation. Unity/UE docs establish workflows, not measured superiority on this PC.

2. Per-area behaviour comparisons

blocker prevents completing the named task; daily friction forces repeated detours, unreliable control or missing workflow; polish is existing coverage to verify or a smaller refinement. A blocker is scoped to its workflow, not a claim the entire engine cannot run.

Effort is agent working time, not calendar duration. Calibration supplied by Islam: full C# bindings ≈9h, macOS port ≈12h, diagnosed render fix ≈1h. Those are reported reference points, not independently recovered session timings. A bounded wiring/bug closure is 1–3h; several gesture/state paths 3–7h; a new cross-layer runtime/rendering contract 8–16h+. Ranges include focused verification and handoff, assume existing primitives can be reused, and carry roughly ±50% uncertainty until exercised. Shared packages appear in several rows: do not sum the table cells.

Why changing and adapting things currently costs too much

Choice controls are independently built in Inspector, nested fields, importer settings, Settings and Hub. Editor, Hub and player have different native-input adapters; the Hub AGENTS file explicitly records copied editor input/frame code. Asset discovery is duplicated between browser extension scanning and the host project scanner. Registry descriptions can remain stale after runtime features land. These are concrete sources of repeated adaptation work, not a case for rewriting the engine.

Use small owned modules: a schema field maps to a widget policy; a drag session emits an application intent; one project index owns asset visibility; one native adapter defines coordinates/text/focus. Keep domain-specific panels for lighting, material, play and installation. Generic controls should make those panels easier to build, not turn every tool into a JSON form. ara-ui/AGENTS.md:30 shell/compound/fields.rs:1 shell/assets.rs:142

3. Editor/product sprint plan

First slice for the preview: close the Mac coordinate candidate with a real platform proof, preflight the missing export cohort, wire camera speed, replace dangerous/unbounded choice and overlay policies, and fix range/drag acceptance. This is a sequence for the existing leads, not a request to launch more build jobs tonight. Reserve GPU/platform acceptance for a quiet machine slot; this audit ran none.

The full closure sprint is approximately 78–120 agent-hours plus 6–10h integration, before deeper renderer/fast-world additions below. With four non-colliding owners the ideal critical path is about 36–50 working hours including integration, not a promise that four agents make it a one-day job. With the two existing leads, serialize each lead's conflicting files. The ≤1h render-fix reference is appropriate only once a cause is diagnosed.

Do not move the finish line to new chrome. A feature is complete when its human gesture, keyboard route and agent command agree; the resulting document/runtime state is right; undo/cancel works; and the accepted capture is linked to that state.

Harness and evidence contract

app/journey.rs:1 already writes per-step captures, layout JSON and journey.json. The existing --verify-journey path uses a hidden native window; --headless is a different path and cannot be used as a substitute for gesture verification. The following is a future acceptance invocation with a matching prebuilt installed cohort and fresh scratch project; it was not run during this audit.

ara-editor.exe <scratch-project> --verify-journey --size 1440x900 --dpi 1 --output <scratch-evidence>
# Repeat focused stories at 2x after the first run passes; do not run concurrent GPU timings.
# Current --verify-journey has a fixed story list; J1–J14 are proposed story additions,
# not existing flags or already passing cases.

Every result must include source/build identity, engine version, profile, DPI/window/drawable extents, starting revision, accepted command/target, expected state, actual state, elapsed time, screenshot/layout names and diagnostic codes. Pass requires every step's effect assertion; finished:true, “no uncommanded buttons,” a compile log substring or a screenshot file alone is insufficient.

After implementation, owners run only their focused check/clippy/test sets and relevant editor/player/UI suites with the shared-PC job cap. Run native GPU proofs serially and use fresh per-run config/crash/profile directories under target or designated scratch evidence. No full workspace integration gate per agent checkpoint. No tests may write tracked evidence; promote captures explicitly.

4. Where Ara should exceed both engines

Ara should compete on reliable shared state and fast verified iteration, not on the claim that established engines have no automation. Unity now documents an in-editor AI assistant and third-party agent plugins; Unreal supports editor Python and other automation. Docs Docs The opportunity is to make human and agent actions semantically identical by construction.

OpportunityWhat already existsNext useful behaviourProof / effort
Live collaboration without disruptionImmediate attributed edits, gesture overlap safety, overwrite notices, turn undo, View/Follow.
activity.rs:1 · shell/agents_panel.rs:1 · ara-host/src/gesture.rs:1
Agent presence shows task/affected objects without moving the human camera; clicking an activity item explains exact fields and offers Undo turn. No accept queue or claims.Human scrubs while agent edits same and different fields; only overlapping op waits, unrelated edit applies; camera stays fixed. 3–5h closure.
Commands with observable completionShared registry and typed ops; editor.commands and editor.command exist. The latter returns queued=true; catalog synthesizes clipboard/play/build state rather than reading all live shell context.
actions.rs:299 · actions.rs:340
Target-aware availability and completion/result token: revision, affected IDs, diagnostics, state proof and artifact links. An agent must distinguish accepted/queued/completed/failed.Run same action from menu, shortcut and MCP; compare ops and result. Disabled action gives actual prerequisite. 3–6h.
Explain values and failuresSchema docs/units/provenance, Problems catalog fixes and why tooling exist.
inspector.rs:1 · shell/log_panels.rs:391
“Why this value / invisible / slow?” links source prefab, latest edit, selected profiler frame and executable typed fix. Open exact object/field without searching logs.One issue packet reproduces cause and effect and supports undo. 4–7h integration, not a new chat panel.
Reproducible multiplayer investigationsDeterministic ticks, per-client conditions, step/input and snapshot infrastructure; export/capture APIs.
ara-play-host/src/params.rs:59
Turn a bug into a replay with seed, client views, network conditions and tick assertion. Agent compares the same world state before/after fix.Host+N story captures divergence and proves correction on replay. 5–9h tool integration after D19 views.

docs/decisions.md:33 · ara/src/commands/init.rs:1
Agent can create, import, move, inspect, play and export without filesystem scavenging or guessing active project. Hub and browser project registries agree.Fresh machine/profile -> pinned engine -> open -> usable scene -> relocated named game, all with result artifacts. Shared with B2/J11/J12.
Performance tied to an editActual frame/GPU captures, compare view, typed history/author/reason.
shell/profiler_panel.rs:386
Select an agent turn and compare frame time/quality before/after; budget regressions name the offending operation and entity/material.Record equal workload/quality with capture identity; do not equate smoother UI paint with faster scene effect. 4–7h integration.

Discussion to settle next: the first acceptance slice, the player-facing folder/executable contract, and who owns the renderer-side orthographic/probe seams. Keep D19/D24/D25/D28 fixed. These are implementation-order choices, not permission to trim engine scope.
